task.description:
Fix migration apply-ordering so GBL-prefixed migrations interleave numerically with NNN_ migrations instead of sorting after all of them.

Root cause is already diagnosed in docs/issues/ISS-0603.json: the apply sort in src/db/migrations.zig (~line 185) uses raw lexicographic std.mem.lessThan on the filename, while migrationOrder() in the same file already encodes the intended ordering (GBL- => +1000 offset). Make the sort use migrationOrder() with filename as a deterministic tiebreak for equal orders.

Verify against a genuinely empty database — this bug is invisible on an already-migrated one. The workspace-2 stack is running: dev DB on localhost:5452, test DB on localhost:5453 (see .env). Create a scratch database to prove the from-empty path, and confirm re-running migrate on an already-migrated DB stays a no-op so existing environments do not regress.
acceptance_criteria: zig build migrate exits 0 against a completely empty database
zig build migrate is a no-op (exits 0, applies nothing) on an already-migrated database
apply order matches the order migrationOrder()-based out-of-order detection enforces
stale 'zero-padded NNN_ prefix ensures numeric order' comment corrected
regression test asserts GBL-119 sorts before 1135
zig build exits 0 with no 'error set' output

result.summary:
Fixed ISS-0603 / GH #467: migration apply order now uses migrationOrder() with a filename tiebreak, so GBL-* migrations interleave numerically with the 1xxx_ series instead of sorting after all of them. The bug existed in TWO runners: src/db/migrations.zig (runForSchema) was the file named in the diagnosis, but `zig build migrate` actually executes a duplicated copy in src/tools/migrate.zig — fixing only the former left the symptom completely unchanged. Both fixed. Out-of-order detection was reworked from a global max-applied watermark to a within-pass 'walked_order' watermark so pre-existing databases (which carry a legacy backlog of pending GBL files below an already-applied 1134) are grandfathered in rather than bricked. Verified against a real pre-existing DB: bpm_dev applied GBL-112..115 after 1134 with no out-of-order error. 4 mutation-tested regression tests added. NOTE: a fresh DB still cannot fully bootstrap due to a SEPARATE circular dependency, filed as ISS-0604 / GH #470 and enqueued.

ISS-0604 / GH #470 (second queued item, authorized by ORCH after independent reproduction) is now ALSO fixed: introduced a declarative `-- scope: public` migration header, honoured by both runners, so public-only migrations are skipped in per-tenant passes. Chose the header over renaming 1135 because the filename is the ledger key (a rename re-runs it everywhere), GBL-135 would collide at order 1135, and an audit found FIVE public-only non-GBL migrations, not one. A misclassified migration now fails loudly with MigrationScopeMismatch. Also deleted src/tools/migrate.zig's duplicate migrationOrder(), closing the ISS-0603 root hazard. Fresh-database bootstrap now reaches 106/106 with exit 0; the run's issue_queue.json is fully drained.
